text: Every element of C belongs to the full subcoalgebra: its underlying submodule is all of C. The tensor square of that full submodule maps onto C⊗C, so the comultiplication stability condition is automatic. This is the whole-object case of the [coalgebra definition](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41), valid even for a zero ambient module. Checks pass: [top_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L165), [comul_mem_tensorSquare_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L50).
Checks the full underlying submodule.
Checks the required tensor-image stability.

Inclusion of subcoalgebras is exactly inclusion of their underlying submodules. The extra information is a proof of comultiplication stability, which imposes no additional ordering condition. This is the subobject interpretation of the [coalgebra axioms](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41); the equivalence compares subsets of the same C, not arbitrary coalgebra maps between different carriers. Checks pass: [le_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L122), [ext](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L129).
Checks inclusion is elementwise containment.
Checks the associated equality criterion.

A subcoalgebra is a submodule D with Δ(D) contained in the image of D⊗D→C⊗C, agreeing over fields with the [coalgebra definition](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). Over general semirings this records stability without presuming that tensor map is injective. A coalgebra on D is constructed separately under explicit flatness assumptions. Checks pass: [comul_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L134), [map_subtype_comulLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Structure.lean#L47).
Checks the exact stored stability condition.
Checks its realization as restricted comultiplication when both flatness hypotheses hold.

This constructor packages a submodule D and the proof that Δ(D) lies in the image of D⊗D as a subcoalgebra. Its elements and scalar operations remain those of D. This implements stability from the [coalgebra definition](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41) without requiring flatness or asserting a coalgebra structure on the subtype. Checks pass: [ofSubmodule_carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L149), [mem_ofSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L154).
Checks the supplied submodule is retained.
Checks membership is unchanged.

The zero subcoalgebra has the zero underlying submodule. Its only element is zero, and linearity gives Δ(0)=0 in the tensor image, so stability is valid over every commutative semiring. This matches the [coalgebra axioms](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41), which impose no multiplicative unit requirement that would exclude this subobject. Checks pass: [mem_bot](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L191), [nonempty_finiteSubcoalgebras](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L79).
Checks its only element is zero.
Checks zero supplies a finitely generated subcoalgebra.

Every comultiplication value lies in the image of the tensor square of the full submodule, because each inclusion from that submodule is surjective. This supplies the full-subcoalgebra case of [coalgebra stability](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). Only the stored comultiplication map is needed here; coassociativity and counit laws are not hypotheses of this lemma. Checks pass: [top_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L165), [mem_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L169).
Checks the resulting full subcoalgebra has the expected carrier.
Checks every ambient element belongs to it.

This projection forgets the comultiplication stability proof and returns the exact underlying submodule of a subcoalgebra. It changes neither elements nor scalar operations, matching the subobject reading of the [coalgebra definition](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). In particular, forgetting this proof does not construct an inherited comultiplication on that module or assume tensor inclusions injective. Checks pass: [mem_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L115), [toSubmodule_carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L119).
Checks membership is preserved.
Checks this is precisely the stored carrier.

The full subcoalgebra forgets to the full submodule, so its carrier is exactly C. Stability holds because tensoring the two surjective full-submodule inclusions remains surjective. This is the ambient-object case of the [coalgebra definition](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41); the equality requires no flatness and includes the case C is zero. Checks pass: [mem_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L169), [comul_mem_tensorSquare_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L50).
Checks all elements belong.
Checks the tensor-image stability used to build top.

An element belongs to a subcoalgebra constructed from D exactly when it belongs to D. The constructor stores D unchanged and merely adds its comultiplication stability proof. This is the expected submodule interpretation of the [coalgebra definition](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41), with no closure operation, quotient or enlargement hidden in the constructor. Checks pass: [ofSubmodule_carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L149), [comul_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L134).
Checks the complete underlying submodule agrees.
Checks the packaged object exposes the required stability.

Two subcoalgebras of the same C are equal if they have exactly the same elements. Their scalar structure is inherited from C, while stability is a property rather than additional selectable data. This agrees with the subobject interpretation of the [coalgebra definition](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41); an abstract isomorphism of different carriers would not suffice. Checks pass: [le_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L122), [mem_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L115).
Checks the associated elementwise inclusion criterion.
Checks the membership predicate is the underlying submodule’s.

The linear span of specified group-like elements is a subcoalgebra: Δ(g)=g⊗g supplies stability on generators, then linearity extends it. Following [EGNO 1.22.13](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47), the native semiring notion explicitly stores ε(g)=1 as well. No multiplication or linear independence of these generators is assumed. Checks pass: [mem_groupLikeSetSpan](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/GroupLike.lean#L85), [groupLikeSetSpan_le](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/GroupLike.lean#L97).
Checks its carrier is exactly the module span.
Checks its least-containing-subcoalgebra property.

Forgetting the subcoalgebra structure of a group-like span gives precisely the module span of the selected underlying elements. The generator equation Δ(g)=g⊗g from [EGNO 1.22.13](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47) makes this span stable without enlarging it. This is a span, not a basis assertion; the selected set may be infinite or linearly dependent. Checks pass: [groupLike_mem_groupLikeSetSpan](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/GroupLike.lean#L91), [groupLikeSetSpan_finite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/GroupLike.lean#L185).
Checks each chosen generator belongs.
Checks a finite generating set gives a finitely generated module.

The subcoalgebra spanned by all group-like elements equals C exactly when those elements span C as a module. This unfolds the shared carrier and the [group-like convention](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). It does not claim every coalgebra has this property, or that a spanning family of group-like elements is automatically independent over a general semiring. Checks pass: [groupLikeSetSpan_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/GroupLike.lean#L77), [top_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L165).
Checks the underlying span formula.
Checks the full-object carrier in the comparison.

A coalgebra equivalence preserves whether group-like elements span the whole carrier. It preserves both Δ(g)=g⊗g and ε(g)=1, hence bijects the group-like elements; its underlying linear equivalence carries their spans onto one another. This implements [EGNO’s group-like definition](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47) and requires a coalgebra equivalence, not merely a linear one. Checks pass: [groupLikeSetSpan_eq_top_iff_span_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/GroupLike.lean#L118), [val_equivOfCoalgEquiv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/GroupLike/Map.lean#L42).
Checks reduction to the module spanning condition.
Checks transported group-like elements have the expected underlying image.

Membership in the subcoalgebra generated by a selected set of group-like elements means membership in their ordinary module span. The span is already stable because each generator satisfies Δ(g)=g⊗g, as in [EGNO 1.22.13](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47). No products, extra elements from coalgebra closure, or finiteness hypothesis are added. Checks pass: [groupLike_mem_groupLikeSetSpan](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/GroupLike.lean#L91), [groupLikeSetSpan_le](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/GroupLike.lean#L97).
Checks the generator case.
Checks the universal property of this span.

Each selected group-like element belongs to the subcoalgebra spanned by that set: it is one of the module-span generators. The [group-like equation](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=47) justifies the span’s coalgebra stability. The stated membership premise is essential; the theorem does not say that the span of an arbitrary selected set contains every group-like element. Checks pass: [mem_groupLikeSetSpan](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/GroupLike.lean#L85), [groupLike_mem_groupLikeSpan](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/GroupLike.lean#L173).
Checks reduction to module-span membership.
Checks the single-generator specialization.

The binary join of subcoalgebras D and E has underlying module D+E. Each summand’s comultiplication lies in the larger tensor image, and linearity proves stability of the sum. This follows the [coalgebra axioms](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). The notation denotes a least upper bound, not whichever operand is larger in a total order. Checks pass: [sup_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Lattice.lean#L75), [mem_sup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Lattice.lean#L81).
Checks the underlying module sum.
Checks membership is a sum of one element from each subcoalgebra.

Subcoalgebras form a semilattice under inclusion, with binary join given by module sum. The two inclusions and least-upper-bound property reduce exactly to those for submodules. This is consistent with [coalgebra stability](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41): each summand’s tensor image sits in the sum’s tensor image, so no flatness assumption is needed. Checks pass: [toSubmodule_le_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L125), [mem_sup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Lattice.lean#L81).
Checks the order comparison used.
Checks the join’s concrete elementwise meaning.

The join of two finitely generated subcoalgebras is finitely generated as an R-module, since its module is their sum and the two finite generating sets together generate it. This is a finite-sum consequence of [coalgebra stability](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). Finite means module generation, not a finite carrier set or finite-dimensional ambient coalgebra. Checks pass: [sup_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Lattice.lean#L75), [sup_mem_finiteSubcoalgebras](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Finite.lean#L85).
Checks the module sum underlying the argument.
Checks closure of the family of finitely generated subcoalgebras.

Forgetting a binary join of subcoalgebras gives the sum of their underlying submodules. This is a defining equality of the join construction, whose stability follows by linearity of Δ and enlargement of tensor images. It matches the [coalgebra axioms](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41); an arbitrary set union would not have the required additive closure. Checks pass: [mem_sup](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Lattice.lean#L81), [finset_sup_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Lattice.lean#L191).
Checks the explicit sum decomposition.
Checks the corresponding finite-join formula.

When both C and D are flat over R, the stable submodule D inherits a coalgebra: tensor injectivity restricts Δ uniquely, and ε restricts directly. Coassociativity and both counit identities match [EGNO 1.20.1](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). Over semirings, flatness here means preservation of injections by tensoring; this structure must be explicitly installed. Checks pass: [map_subtype_comulLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Structure.lean#L47), [counit_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Structure.lean#L143).
Checks the restricted comultiplication recovers the ambient one.
Checks the restricted counit formula.

For the explicitly chosen inherited coalgebra on a flat subcoalgebra of flat C, evaluating the counit on x equals evaluating C’s counit on its underlying element. This is restriction of ε in [EGNO 1.20.1](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). The local structure declaration matters: the formula is not asserted for every conceivable coalgebra structure on the same module. Checks pass: [comul_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Structure.lean#L136), [map_subtype_comulLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Structure.lean#L47).
Checks the companion operation uses the same installed structure.
Checks its comultiplication agrees with the ambient coalgebra.

Including both tensor factors of the constructed Δ_D(x) recovers Δ_C(x). Flatness of C and D makes that tensor map injective, so the stability witness determines a unique value in D⊗D. This is restricted comultiplication in the sense of [EGNO 1.20.1](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41), rather than an unsupported identification of tensor images with submodules. Checks pass: [comul_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Structure.lean#L136), [comul_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Basic.lean#L134).
Checks the constructed map is the inherited coalgebra’s comultiplication.
Checks the required ambient tensor-image membership.

This linear map sends x in D to the unique tensor in D⊗D whose ambient image is Δ_C(x). Stability gives existence; flatness of both C and D gives injectivity and uniqueness. Thus it realizes restricted comultiplication from the [coalgebra definition](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41), without selecting arbitrary representatives from a possibly noninjective tensor map. Checks pass: [map_subtype_comulLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Structure.lean#L47), [comul_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Structure.lean#L136).
Checks the defining ambient-image identity.
Checks the inherited coalgebra uses this map.

After explicitly installing the inherited coalgebra on D, its comultiplication is exactly the previously constructed restricted linear map. Both D and C retain their flatness hypotheses, ensuring the map into D⊗D is well-defined by unique lifting. This realizes the Δ operation in [EGNO 1.20.1](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41); the equality fixes a particular inherited structure. Checks pass: [map_subtype_comulLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Structure.lean#L47), [counit_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcoalgebra/Structure.lean#L143).
Checks the lift recovers the ambient comultiplication.
Checks the matching counit of this same structure.

A floor ring supplies signed integer floor and ceiling for a ring with a linear order. Their comparison laws say z≤floor(x) exactly when z≤x, and ceiling(x)≤z exactly when x≤z. Thus they describe downward and upward integer rounding, including negative inputs; they impose no floating-point approximation or truncation toward zero. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L180).

This structure supplies natural-valued floor and ceiling on a semiring with a partial order. Floor is greatest below x when x≥0, and is zero when x<0; incomparable inputs are not characterized by these floor laws. The docstring’s displayed floor equivalence needs the x≥0 qualification present in Lean. Ceiling is the least natural upper bound. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L59).

Integer-valued floor and ceiling induce natural-valued versions by replacing every negative integer result with zero. Nonnegative results are unchanged. For example, at real −3/2 the integer floor and ceiling are −2 and −1, while both natural-valued results are zero. The conversion therefore preserves the natural rounding laws while deliberately clipping negative outputs. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L351).

The floor and ceiling laws force distinct natural numbers to have distinct images in the semiring. This is Lean’s CharZero condition: injectivity of all natural-number casts, not merely the statement that positive naturals never map to zero. It is derived from the floor structure and partial order, without assuming a field or compatibility of addition with order. Compared with [Aspnes §§4.6–4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L114).

A semiring carrying the stated natural floor and ceiling structure necessarily satisfies 0≤1 in its supplied partial order. This is a consequence of the rounding laws: natural-number inclusion is nondecreasing, so the comparison 0≤1 transfers from the naturals. The declaration records just that comparison, not full compatibility of the order with addition or multiplication. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L112).

The integer ceiling of x is at most an integer z exactly when x itself is at most z. This is the least-integer-upper-bound characterization of ceiling, with z included exactly in the ambient ring for the second comparison. Neither x nor z needs to be nonnegative, so the equivalence also covers signed rounding below zero. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L323).

Integer ceiling is positive exactly when its input is positive. A positive input, however small, needs an integer upper bound of at least 1. Nonpositive inputs have ceiling at most zero; they need not have negative ceiling, as the real input −1/2 has ceiling zero. No assumption of nonnegative input is needed. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L340).

Every input is at most its integer ceiling, after that integer is included in the ambient ring. This is an upper-bound property for signed rounding and applies equally to negative inputs: for example, −3/2≤−1. The ambient structure is a ring with a linear order and the specified floor/ceiling laws; no field hypothesis is required. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L330).

An integer z is strictly below ceiling(x) exactly when z is strictly below x itself. The integer is included exactly in the ambient ring on the right. Both comparisons are strict: if x equals z, neither holds, since integers are fixed by ceiling. Negative integers and negative inputs are included without additional restrictions. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L326).

Natural-number ceiling is positive exactly when the input is positive. At zero and at every negative input it is zero; for a positive real input such as 1/2 it is 1. Unlike signed integer ceiling, this function never returns a negative value. The theorem uses a linear order and the natural floor/ceiling structure. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L169).

If the included natural number n is at most x, then n is at most the natural floor of x. No separate nonnegativity assumption on x is necessary: the premise already places x above a nonnegative natural-number cast. This implication works with a partial order and does not require every pair of ambient values to be comparable. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L149).

For x≥0, a natural number n is at most natural floor(x) exactly when its included value is at most x. The nonnegativity guard matters when n=0: at real x=−1/2, the natural floor is zero, so the left comparison holds while 0≤x fails. The statement allows a partial order. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L146).

A natural number n lies strictly below natural ceiling(x) exactly when its included value lies strictly below x. No nonnegativity assumption on x is needed: for nonpositive inputs the ceiling is zero and both strict comparisons fail. At an exact natural-number boundary, equality gives false on both sides rather than an extra rounding step. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Defs.lean#L165).

Every input is at most its natural-number ceiling, after inclusion into the ambient semiring. This remains true for negative real inputs because their natural ceiling is zero, which is still an upper bound. The theorem requires no sign assumption; it concerns the least natural upper bound, rather than signed integer rounding below zero. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Semiring.lean#L179).

Every input is strictly below one more than its natural floor, even when the input is negative. For a negative real, natural floor is zero, so the inequality simply says x<1. This upper estimate does not imply that natural floor is below x: that familiar lower estimate needs x≥0 because negative inputs are clipped. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Semiring.lean#L63).

Under the stated compatible addition and subtraction assumptions, natural ceiling(a−1) equals natural ceiling(a) minus 1. The right subtraction is in the naturals and stops at zero. The left uses the ambient subtraction: ordinary subtraction for reals, truncated subtraction for naturals. For real a=0, both sides are zero, not −1. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Semiring.lean#L375).

For a nonnegative input x, natural floor(x)=n exactly when n≤x<n+1, using exact natural-number inclusions. The lower endpoint is included and the upper endpoint excluded. Without x≥0 the characterization fails at n=0: negative reals also have natural floor zero, although they do not lie in the interval [0,1). Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Semiring.lean#L50).

For a nonnegative input x, natural floor(x)<n exactly when x<n. The guard handles the natural boundary n=0: at a negative real input the right inequality can hold, but the natural floor is zero and cannot be strictly below zero. Both comparisons are strict, and n is a natural number rather than a signed integer. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Semiring.lean#L41).

Natural floor is nondecreasing: x≤y implies floor(x)≤floor(y). This includes negative inputs, where clipping to zero is compatible with weak order. The conclusion is not strict monotonicity or injectivity; distinct real inputs such as 1/4 and 1/2 both have natural floor zero. The proof uses the supplied linear order to separate the nonpositive case. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Semiring.lean#L87).

If natural floor(x)<n, then x<n, with no sign assumption on x. This one-way implication is stronger in scope than the corresponding equivalence: it still works for negative inputs, while the reverse implication fails when n=0. Indeed, the premise itself forces n>0, so it cannot make the problematic comparison below natural zero. Compared with [Aspnes §4.7](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Semiring.lean#L54).

For a negative fundamental discriminant D=−n, this counts ideal classes of ℚ(√D) by primitive reduced positive definite forms ax²+bxy+cy² with b²−4ac=D. Primitivity means gcd(a,b,c)=1; reduction requires |b|≤a≤c and nonnegative b on the boundary. Natural-number division and square root round down; the proved bounds preserve every representative; each class is counted once, without automorphism weights. See [Sutherland, MIT18.785 ProblemSet9, Problem6, p.8](https://math.mit.edu/classes/18.785/2021fa/ProblemSet9.pdf). It sends (a,b,c) to the class of aℤ+((−b+√D)/2)ℤ, multiplied by √D when a<0. That sign correction is essential: narrow classes identify ideals differing by a principal ideal with a totally positive generator (positive at both real embeddings).
